_what_this_is: The presentations in this vault, arranged by LEVEL. A level is not a depth of explanation, it is a different problem: somebody who does not know what their agents are doing is not looking for a simpler account of premium calculation, they are looking for a list of what their agents did. Each level's solution creates the next level's question, which is what makes the sequence a narrative rather than a menu. So a deck finds the level, answers that level's question, and ends on the question that opens the next one — never answering it, because answering a question nobody has asked is what produces 'this is too much'. Every level now has a deck. tools/decks/<id>.js is a deck's slides, tools/build.py assembles the page, decks.html renders this file.

frame.name: levels
frame.note: This replaced an 'altitude' frame on 4 September. Altitudes said the audience needed a shallower version of the same explanation; levels say the audience has a different problem. The second is right, and only one frame should be in use — this one.
rules: Find the level. Answer that level's question. End on the question that opens the next one, with no answer on the slide.
The customer arrives at each question on their own: the deck's job is to recognise the question, never to plant it.
The value at each level stands alone. Somebody who stops at level 1 has gained something, not bought part of something.
Introduce one term per level, always in the same words, so the vocabulary accumulates instead of arriving at once.
Concepts are introduced in order of attrition, not in order of logic — which is why the policy object comes late even though everything refers to it.

levels.problem: I do not know what my agents are doing
levels.answers: Observation: records of what they did, passive mode, a status block
levels.opens: Some of this looks wrong, and I cannot say why
levels.attrition: none — nobody argues against visibility, and it changes nothing
levels.customer_words: understand what the agents are doing

levels.problem: I can see it and I cannot say what wrong means
levels.answers: The grant measured, the mandate written, the delta rendered
levels.opens: The delta is enormous. What do I do about it?
levels.attrition: some — somebody has to state what they expected, and a written expectation can be wrong in public

levels.problem: The delta is enormous and I cannot close all of it
levels.answers: Bound the parts that matter: bands, limits, refusals
levels.opens: Refusing stops work. Who says yes when somebody needs more?
levels.introduces: the band · the limit · the refusal
levels.attrition: real — it stops work, and the people it stops have a strong voice

levels.problem: A refusal needs a decision and a budget behind it
levels.answers: Draws, a named acceptor, a shared pool
levels.opens: Whose budget is this, and is the price right?
levels.attrition: high — a person's name goes on a decision about risk. This is the politically charged one
levels.customer_words: be sure they are operating within bounds

levels.problem: The pool is shared and mispriced
levels.answers: Premium, experience rating, repricing, the captive
levels.opens: What would have to be true to run one policy, on one agent, for one week?
levels.attrition: highest — it moves money between teams, which is the thing organisations argue about most
levels.customer_words: know what it costs, and what it costs when it goes wrong

decks.title: The problem
decks.audience: a first conversation: the person who owns the risk, or the person who owns the agents
decks.one_line: Opens where almost everybody is standing — agents already running, and no way to say what wrong means — and lands on the delta. Stops there.
decks.ends_on: The delta is enormous. What do I do about it?
decks.stops_before: bands, limits, refusals, pools, premiums, price — none of it appears

decks.title: The map
decks.audience: somebody who has accepted the problem and wants to know what it would take in the estate they actually have
decks.one_line: A companion rather than a step: the same ladder seen from our side — the dependency map whose every absence is a risk entry rather than a blocker, the four layers and their seams, and the rungs, with the one where insurance starts named honestly.
decks.ends_on: Which rung are you pointing at, and what would it take to stand on it?
decks.introduces: the band · the limit · the refusal
decks.stops_before: our roadmap; the last slide is their table, filled in
decks.footer: The map · RiskMandate.ai · a companion to levels 2–3

decks.title: Bounding it
decks.audience: somebody who has seen the delta, tried to close it, and found that some of it is load-bearing
decks.one_line: Stop asking whether the agent may do a thing and start asking how much. The band, the limit, the refusal — and where the check sits, which decides what you are actually buying.
decks.ends_on: Refusing stops work. Who says yes when somebody needs more?
decks.introduces: the band · the limit · the refusal
decks.stops_before: pools, draws, acceptors, budgets, price — a bound needs none of them

decks.title: Who says yes
decks.audience: somebody whose bounds work and who now has a queue — and the roles whose names would go on the answers
decks.one_line: The hardest one. A refusal is a question addressed to somebody: the draw, the acceptor, no deny button, whose name goes on it, and what is signed in advance so the ordinary day never stops.
decks.ends_on: Whose budget is this, and is the price right?
decks.stops_before: the premium, experience rating and repricing — pricing is level 5

decks.title: The insurance model
decks.audience: design partners and builders — and anybody who has reached the pool and the price on their own
decks.one_line: The endgame, whole: grant, mandate, policy, the check, the two modes, the money, risks and acceptance, with real screenshots of the running simulation.
decks.ends_on: What would have to be true to run one policy, on one agent, for one week?
decks.introduces: the draw · the acceptor · the premium
decks.stops_before: nothing. This is the deep one and it should stay as deep as it is — it should be reached, not simplified
decks.footer: Licence to Operate · RiskMandate.ai · level 5 · delivered from an SG/Vault, terms in the vault, run in your browser
